data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services is more resilient to correlated failure than a large redundant service, provided there is substrate diversity.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The 'Shadow Monolith' effect: independent operators all utilize the same underlying managed substrate (e.g., AWS us-east-1), concentrating risk.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Economic Homogeneity: market pressures drive all independent operators toward the same 'industry standard' stack, recreating the monolith's homogeneity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralization breaks the 'fate-sharing' inherent in a single administrative and technical domain. While a monolith has internal redundancy, that redundancy is typically homogeneous (same OS, same config, same orchestration). A decentralized network leverages 'heterogeneous redundancy'\u2014different operators use different versions of software, different cloud providers, and different update cycles\u2014preventing a single latent bug or configuration error from acting as a global kill-switch.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
